A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the WEATHER-5K research work despite the changed title and expanded scope. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original WEATHER-5K forecasting experiments, extreme-event evaluations, efficiency measurements, and dataset analyses, including Tables 2, 3, and 6.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and adds PhysicsFormer, additional comparator results, and a heatwave forecasting case study in Section 4.7.

M1.justification: v2 proposes a dataset and benchmark without a new forecasting model. v3 introduces PhysicsFormer: station and time embeddings, a Transformer encoder–decoder, residual correction of a dynamic-core forecast, and pressure–wind and temporal-smoothness losses.

E1.justification: WEATHER-5K retains the same stations, years, hourly resolution, and five weather variables. Targeted forecasting scenarios change: v2's winter-storm example on unseen stations disappears, while v3 evaluates the 2022 Chongqing heatwave. That heatwave's observations already appeared in v2's dataset analysis.

E2.justification: v3 adds STID, SparseTSF, TimeMixer, WPMixer, MTGNN, Chronos, and Timer to the main comparisons, plus WSSM, UniMTD, and UniTraj in Appendix Table 9. Mamba's accuracy, extreme-event, and efficiency rows disappear; WSSM is a distinct comparator.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce zero-shot evaluation for Chronos and Timer and specify batch size 5600 for STID and MTGNN. The retained chronological split, 48-hour input, four forecast horizons, MAE/MSE/SEDI metrics, and training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused heatwave forecasting comparison, station-versus-ERA5 spatial snapshots, and qualitative examples for new models; the winter-storm and Mamba examples are removed. The existing input-length sensitivity study is retained with fuller explanation, rather than newly performed. No PhysicsFormer component ablation is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark results once and assert stability across seeds without supplying confidence intervals, significance tests, or additional run-count information. Weather-variability bands already appear in v2 and do not establish new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Shared per-horizon errors and extreme-event scores are unchanged, but v3 adds extensive PhysicsFormer and comparator results and removes Mamba results. PhysicsFormer newly reports 24-hour temperature MAE 1.55 and 99.5th-percentile temperature SEDI 30.6%; corresponding HRES values remain 1.76 and 37.4%. The heatwave case adds MAEs of 1.23 for PhysicsFormer and 1.82 for Chronos.

T1.justification: v3 adds formal definitions for residual-plus-dynamics forecasting and pressure–wind and smoothness penalties in Section 4.3. These are limited mathematical formulations without accompanying proofs or a derivation of the dynamic core. The original forecasting definition and SEDI formula remain mathematically equivalent.

C1.justification: v2 centers its contributions on WEATHER-5K, operational benchmarking, and research recommendations. v3 retains these but makes PhysicsFormer a central contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, claiming improved accuracy and physical consistency.

C2.justification: v3 introduces causal explanations attributing PhysicsFormer's performance to its dynamic core and physical losses, and discusses large-model extreme-event capabilities and efficiency. It removes the Mamba-specific interpretation and the limitation concerning insufficient spatial-temporal methods. Station-coverage and imputation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly identifies iTransformer and the fixed 72-hour output for the existing input-length study, explains HRES forecast retrieval and station interpolation, and supplies resource statistics for added models. Existing training, hardware, and repository information is largely retained. PhysicsFormer's core integration procedure and numerical loss weights remain unspecified.

R1.justification: The historical statistical/machine-learning/deep-learning review becomes an MLP/Transformer/GNN/large-model taxonomy, with new physics-informed positioning. References expand to foundation models, graph methods, recent comparators, and physics-informed forecasting, while many classical statistical and machine-learning references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. v3 organizes motivations and contributions into explicit lists, inserts a model section, reorganizes experimental subsections, and moves limitations, recommendations, implementation details, and much dataset analysis into appendices.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main text, introduces radar comparisons, redraws the benchmark and complexity figures, and reorganizes dataset visualizations. Main Table 2 reports horizon averages while full results move to Tables 8–9. Forecast figures expand and their color captions change; the live-demo figure is removed.

improvement.justification: The broader comparator coverage and new heatwave evidence improve the benchmark's usefulness. However, v3 makes PhysicsFormer central without specifying its dynamic-core equations, integration procedure, or loss weights, and without component ablations. Its short-/medium-range HRES comparison claim is broader than the detailed results support: at 72 hours, temperature MAE is 2.22 versus HRES's 1.87. These gains and new weaknesses in reproducibility and claim support prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
